items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: I think that they could -- ... the simple lines that Lester Young played when he played, the melodic continuity. ... Now, I wish that solos -- you take Lester Young's solos, they've not been published, and I think that's another -- mostly the solos he did with Basie, I feel those are his best solos.

ctx.x: So I don't think it's indifference on the part of the young black musician, but I think it's economic pressure. He just doesn't have the time and he's too involved trying to make a living and trying to keep up with the contemporary style, which is quite a bit to keep up with because it's so technical. You know, he'd have to spend his whole time practicing now.

Yeah, right. Thank you for your great defense. I think that's good. We're sitting on opposite sides of the fence and I'm on the side you're talking about, only as a senior citizen now. But I'm concerned with -- I've listened to Prez, when he was living, talk about how he was influenced by some great white players like the great saxophone player that was with Paul Whiteman's band that played C melody saxophone.
Yeah, I keep thinking Teschma ker
